correctness.rationale: Write n=qb+2s and a representation with ell coins as an unordered list of indices in [0,L] summing to s+(q-ell)b/2. Parity and the minimum generator force ell<=q for q>=0 because 2s<2b; the only possible nonnegative representative before q=0 is 2s-b<b. For s=0,1 below the proposed thresholds the ell=q lists are unique when feasible; a shorter eligible list needs index sum at least b+s, beyond its capacity (at most a+1 for the plus cases and at most 2a for the minus cases). For the other residues below threshold there can only be one-coin representations, except the last two minus residues, where q=2 gives the unique unordered pair of sum 2a-1 or 2a. At threshold the displayed pairs or triples are distinct, including at a=2; for the plus a=1 case the middle interval consists of s=2, with pairs (0,2) and (1,1). Adding b to both representations preserves their distinctness and proves exhaustion. The disjoint residue rays give the two rational series, and the threshold sums 3b^2+3b and 3b^2+7b give the asserted genera after subtracting (b-1)/2. The subthreshold counts give exactly the positive singleton sets, excluding the empty representation at zero. An independent exact coin-change check matched thresholds, singleton sets and genera for both families at a=2 through 40 (78 cases).
residual_risks: The finite check corroborates the formulas; the residue exclusion and injection establish the universal claims. The plus extension to a=1 was checked by the proof, not by that separate replay.

evidence: The same-family article treats p-Frobenius maxima for a range of p using lower-layer partition identities and witnesses. Its minus-family §3 uses 4b+2s for m+1<=s<=a and 3b+2s for a+1<=s<=2a, proving minimality in the extremal residue.
Komatsu's general identity needs the complete set of p-Apéry elements; the generalized Fibonacci/Jacobsthal paper uses other generators.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader ranges in p for a scalar maximum do not dominate the complete residue quotient array at p=1. The cited identities support methods and some entries, not every threshold.

evidence: The plus Lemma 4.2 gives the exact witnesses at s=0,1 and s>=a+2; for 2<=s<=a+1 it prints witnesses at 3b+2s from which deleting a common b yields the assigned witnesses at 2b+2s. Those are existence constructions, not all-residue lower bounds.

The minus middle layers need exact two-coin feasibility and uniqueness boundaries, not furnished by the coarser all-residue argument for the maximum. The later index arrays plus the upward injection imply both generating functions; its low-quotient counts imply the singleton loci on a>=4.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the exact published extremal minima and the derivable witnesses. The frozen all-residue result requires additional exclusions and exact low-layer counts; it is not just substitution into the Frobenius-maximum theorem.

originality.rationale: Credit the all-residue minimality and classified singleton loci, not the general Apéry identities, the extreme Frobenius residues or the published witness constructions. The closest publication on the same families establishes the maxima but not the full data: its minus-family middle witnesses can lie in strictly higher layers. The Nov. 8 indexed comparator gives the same arrays and implies the same p=1 consequences for a>=4; this is substantial later indexed coverage, not evidence of an antecedent theorem to the Nov. 2 entry or of independent priority.
residual_risks: Unindexed equivalent low-defect partition tables remain possible; indexed dates do not establish independence or publication priority. The abstract series conversion and part of the witness calculation are not new.

value.rationale: The first repeated representation in each residue is a natural refinement of the p-Frobenius problem for the same motivating families. Knowing each exact onset, and which earlier elements are represented once rather than not at all, answers membership and uniqueness for all n and permits genus and series evaluation; the published maxima cannot give these distinctions.
residual_risks: No claim for higher p, arbitrary arithmetic progressions, or exact denumerants beyond the 0/1/at-least-2 distinction.
